question: Which state of India is at bottom according to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) India Index, published by NITI Aayog in July 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar ranks at the bottom of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) India Index published by NITI Aayog in July 2024.
 
• The SDG India Index evaluates the progress of states and union territories in achieving the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals.
 
• Bihar has consistently been among the lower-ranked states in previous editions of the SDG India Index.
 
• The state's performance is particularly low in areas such as poverty alleviation, quality education, and infrastructure development.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to improve the state's performance through various developmental programs and policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**

 
 
• The SDGs are a set of 17 global goals established by the United Nations to address various social, economic, and environmental challenges.
 
• They were adopted in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
 
• The goals cover areas such as poverty, education, health, gender equality, clean water, and climate action.
 
• Each goal has specific targets and indicators to measure progress.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog) is the premier policy think tank of the Government of India.
 
• It was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• NITI Aayog aims to foster cooperative federalism and promote sustainable development in India.
 
• It plays a critical role in formulating strategic and long-term policies for the country's development.
 
 
 
• **India's SDG Index**
 
 
• The SDG India Index is an annual report published by NITI Aayog to track the progress of Indian states and union territories towards achieving the SDGs.
 
• It uses a range of indicators to assess performance in various areas such as health, education, gender equality, and economic growth.
 
• The index helps identify areas requiring policy intervention and resource allocation.
 
• It encourages competition among states to improve their rankings and overall development.
 
 
 
• **Developmental Challenges in Bihar**
 
 
• Bihar faces several developmental challenges, including high poverty rates, inadequate infrastructure, and low literacy levels.
 
• The state government has initiated various programs to address these issues, such as improving access to quality education and healthcare.
 
• Efforts are also being made to enhance agricultural productivity and create employment opportunities.
 
• Despite these initiatives, significant progress is still needed to achieve the SDGs in Bihar.
